name: Home Assistant
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Home Assistant Core, the home automation platform, in a Python environment. It can't find devices on your network or use USB and Bluetooth devices, which need host networking, and voice and the companion app aren't available; add devices that are reachable by address. The owner account is created at the first start.
startup: export TMPDIR=/home/container/.raptor-tmp; mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"; h=$( (python3 --version; cat .raptor-homeassistant.txt) | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1); if [ "$h" != "$(cat .venv/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing Home Assistant; this takes a few minutes."; rm -rf .venv && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check -q -r .raptor-homeassistant.txt && echo "$h" > .venv/.raptor-installed || exit 1; fi; if ! grep -qs '"is_owner": true' config/.storage/auth; then .venv/bin/python .raptor-owner.py config "{{ADMIN_USERNAME}}" || exit 1; grep -qs '"is_owner": true' config/.storage/auth || { echo "Home Assistant's owner account couldn't be created, so it isn't started: anyone could claim it. Reinstall to try again."; exit 1; }; fi; export SETUP_PORT={{SERVER_PORT}}; if [ -f config/.storage/http ]; then .venv/bin/python -c 'import json, sys; p = "config/.storage/http"; d = json.load(open(p)); [c.update(server_port=int(sys.argv[1])) for c in (d["data"]["stable"], d["data"]["pending"]) if c]; open(p + ".new", "w").write(json.dumps(d, indent=2)); __import__("os").replace(p + ".new", p)' {{SERVER_PORT}} || exit 1; fi; exec .venv/bin/hass --config config --log-no-color --skip-pip-packages pymicro-vad,pyspeex-noise

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Home Assistant: checks the chosen version of Home Assistant Core on PyPI
# and writes it to .raptor-homeassistant.txt; the server installs it (in
# .venv, for the Python version it runs) when it next starts. Writes a
# starting configuration if there's none, and the helper that creates the
# owner account at the first start. The config folder is never overwritten.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

meta=$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "raptor-installer (+https://raptorpanel.net)" https://pypi.org/pypi/homeassistant/json) ||
    fail "PyPI can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
latest=$(jq -r .info.version <<<"$meta")
want="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$want" = latest ] && want="$latest"
jq -e --arg v "$want" '.releases[$v] | length > 0 and all(.yanked | not)' <<<"$meta" >/dev/null ||
    fail "Home Assistant has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $latest, then reinstall."

echo "homeassistant==$want" > .raptor-homeassistant.txt.new
mv -f .raptor-homeassistant.txt.new .raptor-homeassistant.txt

cat > .raptor-owner.py <<'PY'
"""Creates Home Assistant's owner account before its first start, so the
onboarding page can't be claimed by whoever opens it first. Written by
Raptor's install; run with the server's virtual environment."""
import asyncio
import os
import secrets
import sys

from homeassistant import runner
from homeassistant.auth import auth_manager_from_config
from homeassistant.auth.const import GROUP_ID_ADMIN
from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntries
from homeassistant.const import EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_FINAL_WRITE
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
from homeassistant.helpers import device_registry as dr, entity_registry as er


async def main(config_dir: str, username: str) -> None:
    hass = HomeAssistant(os.path.abspath(config_dir))
    hass.config_entries = ConfigEntries(hass, {})
    await hass.config_entries.async_initialize()
    dr.async_setup(hass)
    await asyncio.gather(dr.async_load(hass), er.async_load(hass))
    hass.auth = await auth_manager_from_config(hass, [{"type": "homeassistant"}], [])
    provider = hass.auth.auth_providers[0]
    await provider.async_initialize()
    if not any(u.is_owner for u in await hass.auth.async_get_users()):
        password = os.environ.get("ADMIN_PASSWORD") or ""
        if not password:
            password = secrets.token_urlsafe(15)
            print(f"Home Assistant's owner is {username}, with the password {password}. Log in and change it.")
        if username in [c["username"] for c in provider.data.users]:
            provider.data.change_password(username, password)
        else:
            provider.data.add_auth(username, password)
        await provider.data.async_save()
        credentials = await provider.async_get_or_create_credentials({"username": username})
        user = await hass.auth.async_create_user(username, group_ids=[GROUP_ID_ADMIN])
        await hass.auth.async_link_user(user, credentials)
        print(f"Created Home Assistant's owner account, {username}.")
    # Home Assistant writes its stores when it shuts down; this one never
    # started, so ask them to write now.
    hass.bus.async_fire(EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_FINAL_WRITE)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    await hass.async_stop()


asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]), loop_factory=runner.create_event_loop)
PY

mkdir -p config
if [ ! -f config/configuration.yaml ]; then
    cat > config/configuration.yaml <<'YAML'
# Home Assistant's configuration: https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/
# This is default_config without what can't work in a container (finding
# devices on your network: dhcp, ssdp, zeroconf; USB and Bluetooth devices)
# and the integrations that call out on their own (cloud,
# homeassistant_alerts). Voice (Assist) and the companion app (mobile_app)
# need packages that have to be compiled, and the server has no compiler.
# Add any of them back here if you need them.
config:
conversation:
energy:
file:
frontend:
history:
logbook:
media_source:
my:
sun:
usage_prediction:
webhook:

automation: !include automations.yaml
script: !include scripts.yaml
scene: !include scenes.yaml

# Warnings and errors in the console, plus when Home Assistant has started.
logger:
  default: warning
  logs:
    homeassistant.bootstrap: info
YAML
    [ -f config/automations.yaml ] || echo "[]" > config/automations.yaml
    touch config/scripts.yaml config/scenes.yaml
    echo "Wrote a starting configuration.yaml."
fi
echo "Installed Home Assistant $want; it's set up when the server starts."
